# Weegloo — Webhook + WriteBack (async external API jobs)

## When to use

- The product must call an **external HTTP API** (LLM, image generation, moderation, search indexer, etc.) **without** hosting a dedicated backend worker.
- The user wants **“create a job → wait for result”** from the browser: frontend creates **Content**, then **polls** by `sys.id` until a **response** field is filled.
- You are provisioning **ContentType + Webhook + WriteBack** together for a new integration.

Canonical behavior and JSON examples: [Webhook — WriteBack](https://docs.weegloo.com/en-US/getting-started/core-concepts/deployment-and-integration/webhook/#feeding-the-response-back-in-writeback). API shapes: CMA OpenAPI **Webhook** (via **`weegloo-api-endpoints`** docs discovery).

## Mental model

1. **Webhook** — on a Space event (e.g. `Content.Create`), Weegloo **calls your external URL** (optionally reshaped with **Transformation**).
2. **WriteBack** — if the external call returns **2xx**, Weegloo runs **`writeBacks`** to **create / update / delete** **Content** or **Media** inside the Space, using **`{ /response/... }`** (API body) and **`{ /payload/... }`** (triggering resource).
3. **Job record** — declare a **job ContentType** whose fields hold the **request** (what the user sent) and **response** (what came back). The frontend **creates** one Content row, then **polls** that row until **response** is populated.

Sensitive values (API keys) belong in Webhook **`Headers`** as **secret entries** — secret Header values are **encrypted and stored securely** by Weegloo. Put keys there, not in Content fields.

**Role design is part of the integration.** Job rows hold **request** (user input) and **response** (filled by **WriteBack** after the external API succeeds). End users must be able to **create** a job, but must **not** read, edit, or delete **another user’s** job — and must **not** forge a completed **`response`** on their own or others’ rows. Configure **`SpaceRole`** (Weegloo User + CMA/CDA) or **`ServiceUserRole`** (Service User + ACMA/ACDA) accordingly — see **§ Role design for job Request / Response Content** below.

## Agent workflow (do this in order)

Copy and track:

```
- [ ] 1. Read weegloo-create-content-type + weegloo-default-locale (field types, locale buckets)
- [ ] 2. Design job ContentType (request + response fields)
- [ ] 3. cma_CreateContentType (note sys.id)
- [ ] 4. **Configure role(s)** for job Content — **Create** open on job ContentType; **Read / Edit / Delete** (and related actions you grant) **only** with **`createdBy.sys.id": ":self"`** on that ContentType (**§ Role design**; **`weegloo-space-role`**)
- [ ] 5. Ensure MCP exposes Webhook tools (group=extra or group=all — see below)
- [ ] 6. Create Webhook: ONE topic, filter to job ContentType, URL + secret Headers + Transformation + writeBacks
- [ ] 7. Document frontend: create job → poll by sys.id until response set (caller may **Read** only **own** rows per role)
- [ ] 8. Verify: user A cannot **Read** or **Edit** user B’s job; user cannot **Edit** `response` to fake completion (WriteBack still updates via platform)
```

### MCP tools

Webhook CRUD lives in the **`extra`** MCP tool group (or **`all`**). If tools are missing, configure the Weegloo MCP server with `?group=extra` or `?group=all` per project README — do **not** call CMA HTTP for Webhooks from the agent.

Use **`cma_*Webhook*`** MCP tools only (same rule as **`weegloo-global-rules`**).

## Step 1 — Job ContentType

Typical fields (adapt names to the product):

| Field | Type | `localized` | Role |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Request input | `ShortText` / `LongText` / `RichText` | usually `false` for job state | User prompt, payload text, or parameters |
| Response | `LongText` or **`Refer` → Media** | usually `false` | External API result; empty until WriteBack runs |

- **Text APIs** — store JSON or plain text in a **LongText** `response` field via WriteBack **`$content` `update`**.
- **Binary / image APIs** — use **`Refer` (Media)** for `response`; in WriteBack set the field to **`{ "$media": { "source": "{ /response/... }", "encoding": "url" } }`** (or `base64`) so Weegloo ingests the file and stores a Media reference.

Follow **`weegloo-create-content-type`** for RichText vs LongText defaults. Follow **`weegloo-default-locale`**: on **Content create**, every populated field needs the **default locale** bucket (e.g. `"en-US": "..."`).

Leave **`response`** empty at create time. Only **WriteBack** (after a **2xx** external response) should populate it — role rules below stop users from patching **`response`** directly to impersonate a finished job.

## Role design for job Request / Response Content (mandatory)

When the job ContentType is the **Request / Response carrier** for an external API (this skill’s main pattern), **always** split permissions on the role’s **`content`** map:

| Action on job **Content** | Typical rule | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **`Create`** | **Allow** for the job **ContentType** — **no** `createdBy` filter (or only `contentType` filter) | Any permitted caller may **submit** a new job (request payload). |
| **`Read`** | **Allow** with **`contentType`** + **`createdBy.sys.id": ":self"`** | Poll and inspect **only your own** job row (`sys.id` you created). |
| **`Edit`** | **Allow** with **`contentType`** + **`createdBy.sys.id": ":self"`** | Optional user edits to **request** fields on **own** rows only; blocks forging **`response`** on others’ rows or tampering with others’ results. |
| **`Delete`** | Same **`:self`** + **ContentType** filter if delete is granted | Users may cancel **own** jobs only. |
| **`Publish`** / **`Unpublish`** | Apply the same **`:self`** + **ContentType** pattern if the role grants them | Avoid cross-user publish of job state. |

Use the reserved id **`:self`** (not a hard-coded User id) so the filter tracks **whoever is authenticated** — see **`weegloo-space-role`**.

**Who gets which role**

| Caller | Role resource | Assign via |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Weegloo User (console, custom admin, PAT) | **`SpaceRole`** | Space membership and/or **`DeliveryAccessToken`** for CDA poll |
| Service User (product sign-up) | **`ServiceUserRole`** | **`ServiceLogin.sys.defaultRole`** / **`ServiceUser.roleOverride`** |

Create or update roles with **`cma_CreateSpaceRole`** / **`cma_CreateServiceUserRole`** (MCP). Full filter shapes and mistakes: **`weegloo-space-role`**.

**Illustrative `content` rules** (job ContentType id `<jobCtId>` — add **`media`** / **`contentType`** maps separately if needed):

```json
"content": {
  "Create": {
    "Allow": [
      {
        "contentType": {
          "sys": {
            "type": "Refer",
            "id": "<jobCtId>",
            "targetType": "ContentType"
          }
        }
      }
    ]
  },
  "Read": {
    "Allow": [
      {
        "contentType": {
          "sys": {
            "type": "Refer",
            "id": "<jobCtId>",
            "targetType": "ContentType"
          }
        },
        "createdBy": {
          "sys": {
            "type": "Refer",
            "id": ":self",
            "targetType": "User"
          }
        }
      }
    ]
  },
  "Edit": {
    "Allow": [
      {
        "contentType": {
          "sys": {
            "type": "Refer",
            "id": "<jobCtId>",
            "targetType": "ContentType"
          }
        },
        "createdBy": {
          "sys": {
            "type": "Refer",
            "id": ":self",
            "targetType": "User"
          }
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Mirror **`Delete`** (and any other granted actions) with the same **`contentType`** + **`:self`** pair.

**What this does *not* block**

- **WriteBack** runs as the **platform** after a successful external call. It can **`update`** the triggering Content’s **`response`** even though the end user has no **Edit** on another member’s row. That is intended.
- **Create** stays broad so the Webhook pipeline can start from a new row per user request.

**What goes wrong without this**

- **Open `Read` on job Content** → any user polls or leaks **another user’s** request/response (prompts, generated media, PII).
- **Open `Edit` on job Content** → a user sets **`response`** manually and bypasses the external API (fake “completed” job).
- **Open `Delete` on others’ jobs** → griefing or denial of service on shared Spaces.

**CDA / DeliveryAccessToken:** if anonymous visitors poll jobs, the token’s **`SpaceRole`** must still use **`:self`** on **Read** for the job ContentType — a shared token does **not** add per-browser identity. Per-member jobs belong on **ACDA** + **`ServiceUserRole`**, not public CDA, unless each visitor is a distinct authenticated Weegloo User.

## Step 2 — Webhook configuration

| Setting | Guidance |
| --- | --- |
| **Topics** | Subscribe to **exactly one** topic for WriteBack flows — usually **`Content.Create`**. Do **not** also subscribe to `Content.Publish` on the same Webhook (duplicate external calls). |
| **Filters** | Restrict to the job ContentType: `doc`: `sys.contentType.sys.id`, `op`: `EQ`, `value`: `<job ContentType sys.id>`. |
| **URL** | External API endpoint. |
| **Headers** | Auth / API keys here as **secret** entries — encrypted and stored securely by Weegloo. Put keys here, not in Content. |
| **Transformation** | Map `{ /payload/fields/<name>/<default-locale> }` (and `{ /payload/sys/id }`) into the body/URL the external API expects. JSON Pointer syntax matches docs. |
| **writeBacks** | Almost always **`$content` `action`: `update`** with **`target` omitted** so the **triggering** Content is updated. |

WriteBack runs only on **2xx** external responses. Non-2xx → no WriteBack; `writeBackResults` stays empty.

## Step 3 — WriteBack (update triggering Content)

**Pattern A — text response on the same Content**

```json
{
  "writeBacks": [
    {
      "$content": {
        "action": "update",
        "fields": {
          "response": "{ /response/choices/0/message/content }"
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Adjust the pointer to match the real external JSON. Use literal + pointer mix when needed: `"Done: { /payload/sys/id }"`.

**Pattern B — image (or file) into a Media Refer field**

`$media` **`encoding`** must match what the external API returns:

| `encoding` | When to use | `source` pointer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **`base64`** | **Default for image LLMs** — body contains base64 bytes (often under `b64_json`, `image`, `data`, etc.) | `{ /response/data/0/b64_json }` (adjust path to provider JSON) |
| **`url`** | Provider returns a **download URL**; Weegloo fetches the bytes | `{ /response/data/0/url }` |

`binary` is **not** supported. Strip `data:image/png;base64,` prefixes in the API response if present — the pointer must resolve to **raw base64** (or use a provider field that already does).

**B1 — base64 (typical for DALL·E-style APIs)**

```json
{
  "writeBacks": [
    {
      "$content": {
        "action": "update",
        "fields": {
          "response": {
            "$media": {
              "source": "{ /response/data/0/b64_json }",
              "encoding": "base64"
            }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

**B2 — URL (provider returns a hosted image link)**

```json
{
  "writeBacks": [
    {
      "$content": {
        "action": "update",
        "fields": {
          "response": {
            "$media": {
              "source": "{ /response/data/0/url }",
              "encoding": "url"
            }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Standalone **`$media` `create`** (no Content field) uses the same `source` / `encoding` pair; optional **`title`** / **`description`** value expressions apply on create only.

- **`$content` `update`** with no **`target`** → updates the Content that fired the Webhook.
- Default **`publish`: true** on create/update → updated job Content is **published** and readable on **CDA** (see **`weegloo-cda-publish`**). Use **`publish: false`** only when the product should keep drafts.

**Alternative** — WriteBack **`create`** a *separate* result ContentType (docs examples). Prefer **single job row + update** when the frontend already holds one `sys.id` to poll.

### Locale (Transformation + WriteBack)

Job ContentTypes usually use **`localized: false`** — one value per field, always stored under the Space **default locale** bucket in CMA (see **`weegloo-default-locale`**).

| Layer | What to set |
| --- | --- |
| **Transformation** (read trigger Content) | Point at the default locale segment: `{ /payload/fields/prompt/en-US }` — replace `en-US` with the Space default locale code (`ko-KR`, etc.). |
| **Frontend Content create** | Every field value uses that same default locale key, e.g. `"fields": { "prompt": { "en-US": "a cat" } }`. |
| **WriteBack `$content` `update`** on `localized: false` fields | Omit **`locale`** — values land in the default locale automatically. |
| **WriteBack `$content` `create` / `update` on `localized: true` fields** | Set **`locale`** to a literal (`"ko-KR"`) or a pointer (e.g. `"{ /payload/sys/locale }"`) so `fields` map to the intended bucket. |
| **WriteBack `$media` `create`** | Optional **`locale`** — Locale for the ingested file and optional `title` / `description`; omit for default locale. |

CDA reads use the delivery **`locale`** query parameter as usual; job polling by `sys.id` is unchanged.

## Reference example — prompt → LLM image → poll Media field

**Goal:** User submits a **prompt**; backend calls an image LLM; frontend polls until **`response`** (Media Refer) is set.

1. **ContentType** `ImageGenerationJob` (example):
   - `prompt` — `ShortText` or `LongText`, `localized: false`
   - `response` — `Refer` → **Media**, `localized: false`
2. **Role** — **`Create`** on `ImageGenerationJob` Content; **`Read`** / **`Edit`** / **`Delete`** with **`createdBy.sys.id": ":self"`** (§ Role design).
3. **Webhook**
   - Topic: **`Content.Create`**
   - Filter: `sys.contentType.sys.id` **EQ** `<ImageGenerationJob sys.id>`
   - **Transformation**: POST body `{ "prompt": "{ /payload/fields/prompt/en-US }" }` (use the space default locale code)
   - **Headers**: provider API key (secret)
4. **WriteBack**: Pattern **B1** (`encoding: base64`) unless the provider returns a URL — then Pattern **B2**. Map `source` to the provider’s base64 or URL field (e.g. `b64_json`, `image`, `data[0].url`).
5. **Frontend**
   - **Create** job Content via **CMA** (or ACMA if members create jobs — see **`weegloo-service-architecture`**).
   - Save returned **`sys.id`**.
   - **Poll** **CDA** (public site + DeliveryAccessToken) or **CMA** GET until `fields.response` references a Media (or use **`weegloo-api-query-optimization`** `sys.id` single fetch).
   - Stop polling when `response` is non-empty / Media link present; handle timeout UX in the app.

## Frontend integration notes

- **Create** returns `sys.id` immediately; external work is **asynchronous**.
- Poll interval/backoff is app-defined (e.g. 1–3s, max duration).
- Delivery read path needs a **published** job row — WriteBack update with default publish satisfies **CDA** polling.
- For **draft-only** jobs, poll **CMA** instead or set WriteBack **`publish: false`** and read via CMA.

## Pitfalls (from product docs)

| Topic | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| Topics | **One** topic per WriteBack Webhook. |
| Logic | No conditionals/loops in WriteBack — only pointer extraction. |
| Chaining | WriteBack changes emit events; other Webhooks may fire — platform blocks infinite loops on create/update. |
| Reliability | **At-most-once** — a failed mid-flight operation may be lost; design idempotent external APIs where cost matters. |
| Security (roles) | **Mandatory** for Request/Response job ContentTypes: **`Create`** without `createdBy` filter; **`Read` / `Edit` / `Delete`** (and publish actions you grant) with **`contentType`** + **`createdBy.sys.id": ":self"`**. Prevents cross-user job snooping and manual **`response`** forgery. **`weegloo-space-role`**. |
| Media | `$media` has no **`update`** action. |
| Plain-text API body | `{ /response }` is whole body; sub-paths need JSON. |

## Debugging

- Inspect **WebhookCallDetail** / **`sys.writeBackResults`** on the call (per-operation `Success` / `Failed` / `Skipped`, `targetId`).
- External non-2xx → WriteBack skipped entirely.
- Wrong JSON Pointer → field stays empty; fix Transformation or WriteBack paths against a sample response.

## Related skills

- **`weegloo-create-content-type`** — job ContentType fields
- **`weegloo-default-locale`** — create payloads and pointer paths
- **`weegloo-cda-publish`** — why CDA sees WriteBack results
- **`weegloo-api-query-optimization`** — poll single Content by `sys.id`
- **`weegloo-service-architecture`** — CMA vs ACMA for who creates jobs
- **`weegloo-delivery-access-token`** — CDA poll from the browser
- **`weegloo-space-role`** — `createdBy` / `:self` on SpaceRole rules

rules.content:
---
id: weegloo-api-endpoints
type: rule
title: Weegloo API Base URLs (for development code)
description: >
  CMA, CDA, Upload, ACMA, ACDA, and Auth (auth.weegloo.com — ServiceLogin OAuth) base URLs,
  API-Docs links, vendor JSON media type / Accept header rules, the two login models in Weegloo
  (Weegloo User vs Service User) and the API surfaces each token authorizes, CDA published-only
  semantics (create/update/unpublish/delete), ACMA auto-publish on create and implicit unpublish
  on delete (no separate publish/unpublish vs CMA), Media list mimeGroup query filters,
  ServiceLogin Bearer Token scope (ACMA/ACDA only), ACMA `GET /v1/me` for current ServiceUser
  (not `/spaces/{spaceId}/me`), ACMA ownership + `isAdmin`, ACDA per-member read scope with
  `ServiceUser.roleOverride`, service-type → API selection pointer, and MCP vs direct API
  usage. Follow when calling Weegloo APIs from application code.
---

rules:
  - section: AI Agent vs application code (mandatory)
    items:
      - **AI Agent (Cursor, Claude, etc.)** must **not** call these HTTP APIs directly. Use **Weegloo MCP tools** only.
      - **Application / development code** (frontend, backend, scripts) may call the APIs using the base URLs and paths documented below.
      - APIs are for **implementation in project code**; agents integrate via **MCP**, not raw REST calls.

  - section: Two login models (read this before picking an API)
    items:
      - Weegloo has **two completely separate identity systems**. The API a caller may use is determined by which identity issued the token.
      - **Weegloo User** — a Weegloo **platform account** (Space owner or **invited** Space member). **No self-signup** — onboarding is by invitation only. Bearer Token (a **Personal Access Token** for server/CI, or the token returned by the **Weegloo Console FE login popup** for browser admin UIs) authorizes **CMA**, **Upload**, and **CDA**. Mechanics: **`weegloo-user-login`** skill.
      - **Service User** — an end-user of the product the Space ships, signed in via **ServiceLogin** (e.g. Google OAuth). **Anyone may sign up**. Bearer Token (issued via `auth.weegloo.com`) authorizes **ACMA**, **ACDA**, and **Upload** — never CMA / CDA. The Upload path lets a member contribute media: **Upload** with the ServiceLogin Bearer, then **ACMA** Media create to attach the resulting asset (CMA Media is still Weegloo-User-only). Mechanics: **`weegloo-service-login`** skill (wire protocol + SDK: **`weegloo-service-login-sdk`**).
      - **Tokens do not cross identity boundaries.** A Service User Bearer must never be sent to CMA / CDA; a Weegloo User Bearer is not a valid caller on ACMA / ACDA. **Upload** is the one shared surface — both Weegloo User and Service User Bearers are accepted; the Media resource that follows is created on **CMA** (Weegloo User) or **ACMA** (Service User), matching the identity that did the upload.

  - section: Base URL by API Type (never guess or infer)
    items:
      - Weegloo APIs include **CMA**, **CDA**, **Upload**, and when the product runs its own end-user (Service User) directory, **ACMA** and **ACDA** instead of CMA/CDA for those flows.
      - **CMA** (Content Management API): Read, create, update, delete as a **Weegloo User**. Base URL: `https://cma.weegloo.com`
      - **CDA** (Content Delivery API): Cache-based, read-only delivery of **published** resources. Base URL: `https://cda.weegloo.com`
      - **Upload**: File uploads. Accepts both a **Weegloo User** Bearer (followed by **CMA** Media create) and a **Service User** Bearer (followed by **ACMA** Media create). Base URL: `https://upload.weegloo.com`. **REST mechanics (multipart/binary endpoints, the temporary `Upload.sys.id`, and the Media/WebHosting create payloads that consume it) live in the `weegloo-upload-api` skill.** The raw REST upload endpoints are for **application code**; when the **agent** uploads a local file it uses the **`weegloo-upload` MCP** instead (the Upload OpenAPI states the REST endpoints are "not for the MCP protocol"). Do not conflate the two.
      - **ACMA** (App Content Management API): Use when the product uses **its own end-user (Service User) directory** instead of having every writer be a Weegloo platform account. In that case use **ACMA instead of CMA** for those member-scoped operations. Base URL: `https://acma.weegloo.com`
      - **ACDA** (App Content Delivery API): Same scenario—**Service Users**. Use **ACDA instead of CDA** for delivery/read paths that map to that model. Base URL: `https://acda.weegloo.com`
      - **Auth** (ServiceLogin OAuth): Sign-in entry, token exchange, refresh, and logout for **Service Users** (`ServiceUser`). Base URL: `https://auth.weegloo.com`. **Endpoint mechanics, exact paths, request/response shapes, and the official browser SDK live in the `weegloo-service-login-sdk` skill** — do not re-derive them ad hoc.
      - API paths typically use `/v1/...`, e.g. `https://cda.weegloo.com/v1` for CDA.

  - section: Accept header and JSON media type (mandatory for HTTP clients)
    items:
      - Weegloo API responses use **`Content-Type: application/vnd.com.weegloo.v1+json;charset=UTF-8`**, **not** plain `application/json`.
      - **Do not** send **`Accept: application/json`**. Negotiation against that value does **not** match Weegloo’s vendor media type and can cause **406 Not Acceptable** or other failures.
      - **Preferred:** **omit** the `Accept` header on requests (e.g. `fetch` without `Accept`) unless you have a specific reason to set it.
      - **If** you must set `Accept`, use the same vendor type as the API: **`application/vnd.com.weegloo.v1+json;charset=UTF-8`** (exactly—with charset as the service expects).
      - When implementing wrappers (axios instances, shared `fetch` helpers), ensure defaults do **not** force `Accept: application/json`. Strip or override client-wide JSON defaults for Weegloo hosts.

  - section: API documentation (OpenAPI) per API
    items:
      - **Canonical URLs only here.** Do **not** paste duplicate **`docs.weegloo.com/api-docs/...`** links into other `.cursor` rules or skills—reference **this section** so paths stay maintainable.
      - **API docs** (OpenAPI / operations—human browsing):
      - **CMA**: `https://docs.weegloo.com/api-docs/cma`
      - **CDA**: `https://docs.weegloo.com/api-docs/cda`
      - **Upload**: `https://docs.weegloo.com/api-docs/upload`
      - **ACMA**: `https://docs.weegloo.com/api-docs/acma`
      - **ACDA**: `https://docs.weegloo.com/api-docs/acda`
      - Use these for **`FieldValidation`**, **`CreateSpaceRole`**, **`CreateDeliveryAccessToken`**, **`CreateContentType`**, **`PATCH`** paths, query parameters, and any operation-level detail.

  - section: SpaceRole & ServiceUserRole — permission filters (`createdBy`, `:self`)
    items:
      - **`SpaceRole`** and **`ServiceUserRole`** scope **`contentType`**, **`content`**, and **`media`** actions with optional rules: **`contentType`**, **`createdBy`**, **`tag`**. Empty **`Allow`** / **`Deny`** rule arrays `[]` mean no filter (all resources of that kind).
      - **`createdBy.sys.id`** limits access to resources created by a specific user. Use a **fixed** id (e.g. `"12345"`) for one known creator; use the reserved value **`:self`** so the filter resolves to the **currently authenticated caller** (Weegloo **User** for CMA/CDA + **SpaceRole**; **`ServiceUser`** for ACMA/ACDA + **ServiceUserRole**) — “only what I created,” not a directory id.
      - **Per-user private Content (Weegloo User):** on the role’s **`content`** map, grant the action (e.g. **`Read`**) with **`Allow`** containing both a **`contentType`** `Refer` and **`createdBy.sys.id": ":self"`**. Full recipes and mistakes: **`weegloo-space-role`** skill.
      - **Webhook job Request/Response Content:** **`Create`** allowed on the job **ContentType** without **`createdBy`**; **`Read`**, **`Edit`**, **`Delete`** (and publish actions you grant) require **`contentType`** + **`createdBy.sys.id": ":self"`** so only the submitting user sees or mutates their job — **WriteBack** still fills **`response`** platform-side. **`weegloo-webhook-writeback`** skill.
      - **Canonical reference (overview + structure):** `https://docs.weegloo.com/en-US/api/reference/cma/space-role/` — **ServiceUserRole** uses the same filter keys on ACMA; see CMA **`CreateServiceUserRole`** in OpenAPI above.

  - section: Weegloo documentation (general, agent-readable) — look here when unsure
    items:
      - Separate from the **API Swagger specs** above, **`docs.weegloo.com`** hosts the **general Weegloo documentation**: concept guides, how-tos, per-resource references, locale/search/filter behavior, error meanings, FAQ, and more.
      - **When in doubt, read the docs — do not guess.** If you are not certain how something works or behaves (a query/filter parameter, `select`/`include` response shape, locale rules, an error code, a publish/version semantic, or any Weegloo concept), look it up here **before** acting. Treat these docs as the source of truth over assumptions.
      - **Discover the path, do not guess (mandatory order).** (1) Fetch the index **`https://docs.weegloo.com/llms.txt`** first — it lists every page with its **`.md`** link. (2) Use only an **exact** path from the index, or a link inside a valid Weegloo Markdown page you already fetched. (3) Fetch that exact path with **`.md`** appended. **You may not fetch a `.md` URL unless you can point to where its path came from** — a line in `llms.txt` or a real in-doc link. Do not hand-build, rename, pluralize, or try nearby doc paths; the **`.md`** suffix is **not** a path-discovery mechanism. (The docs site is a SPA, so an unknown path returns the app shell, not Markdown.)
      - **Wrong-path signal — re-derive, do not thrash.** If a docs fetch returns HTML, a SPA shell (`<!doctype html>` or a `<div id="root">` app root), a redirect to the app, or **403 / 404**, the **path is wrong or absent**. Go back to `llms.txt`, find the exact path, then fetch its **`.md`**. Do **not** retry path variants, and do **not** switch fetch tools to diagnose the same guessed path.
      - **Fetch hygiene (the tool is secondary).** Path validity matters more than the fetch tool — WebFetch and curl both return the wrong thing for a guessed or nonexistent path. A valid Markdown fetch starts with Markdown (a heading or frontmatter), **not** `<!doctype html>` or a SPA root element; if you see the shell, re-check `llms.txt` **before** changing tools. For an **npm package's** docs, prefer **`npm view <pkg> readme`** (or **`npm view <pkg>`**), or **Read `node_modules/<pkg>/README.md`** if the package is installed — don't fetch the rendered npm web page.
      - **Alternative source (Context7).** If available, query the indexed copy — library id **`/websites/weegloo`** via the Context7 MCP (`resolve-library-id` → `query-docs`), or **`https://context7.com/websites/weegloo/llms.txt?topic=...`**. Context7 mirrors `docs.weegloo.com` (may lag slightly); when results conflict, the first-party **`.md`** wins. Still resolve the page from the index, not by guessing.
      - **Swagger vs general docs:** use the **API Swagger specs** (section above) for exact schemas/validation; use these **`.md`** docs for concepts, behavior, examples, and anything the schema alone does not pin down.

  - section: CMA vs CDA selection (Weegloo User identity)
    items:
      - Most web services only need **read** access when content is managed in Weegloo Console. Use **CDA** (typically with a **`DeliveryAccessToken`**) in that case.
      - CMA supports full CRUD and is the right surface for a **Weegloo User** session (PAT or console FE login — see **`weegloo-user-login`**); CDA is preferable for read-only public/browser use because the **`DeliveryAccessToken`** can be scoped to a least-privilege `SpaceRole`.
      - A Weegloo User Bearer Token also authorizes CDA (read), but for production browser delivery use a **`DeliveryAccessToken`** so the client is least-privileged. Detail: **`weegloo-user-login`** and **`weegloo-delivery-access-token`**.
      - Do not confuse CMA and CDA. Use CDA for read-only delivery; CMA for management operations.

  - section: CDA — published snapshot only (vs CMA drafts)
    items:
      - **CDA** returns **only published** resources. Field values are the **published snapshot** at the time of publish—not necessarily the latest **draft** visible in CMA.
      - **Appear on CDA:** **Create** the resource in **CMA** (or the console), then **Publish**. Until publish completes, the resource is **not** visible on **CDA**.
      - **Refresh CDA after edits:** **Update** in **CMA**, then **Publish** again. CDA reflects changes **only after** that publish (subject to cache; see product docs for invalidation).
      - **Unpublish** removes the resource from **CDA** (delivery) but does **not** delete it from **CMA**—it may remain as an unpublished draft. To **remove the resource entirely**, call the **Delete** API (or equivalent management operation) per **OpenAPI**, not “unpublish only.”
      - **ACDA** follows the same **published-delivery** idea for app-managed spaces—confirm operation names in **API docs** (see **API documentation** section above).
      - Narrative and troubleshooting: **`weegloo-cda-publish`** skill.

  - section: ACMA / ACDA vs CMA / CDA (Service User identity)
    items:
      - Most web services only need **read** access, since content create/update/delete is managed in Weegloo Console. Use **CDA** or **ACDA** in that case.
      - CMA/ACMA supports read, create, update, and delete, but CDA is preferable for read-only use due to its cache-based design.
      - Do not confuse CMA/ACMA and CDA/ACDA. Use CDA/ACDA for read-only, CMA/ACMA for management operations.
      - When the product runs its **own Service User directory** (open sign-up via **ServiceLogin**, not the Weegloo platform-account model), **do not use CMA/CDA** for member-scoped features—use **ACMA** and **ACDA** as documented in **API docs** and product docs.
      - **ACMA** replaces **CMA** for that integration style; **ACDA** replaces **CDA** for the corresponding delivery/read usage.
      - **ACMA publish / delete vs CMA:** On **ACMA**, **Create** **automatically publishes**—do **not** rely on a separate **Publish** call after create (contrast **CMA**, where delivery generally requires **Publish** after create/update). On **ACMA**, **Delete** **automatically unpublishes**—do **not** call **Unpublish** before delete. Narrative: **`weegloo-cda-publish`** skill.
      - **Caller identity (mandatory):** ACMA and ACDA accept **only** a **Bearer Token issued by `ServiceLogin`** (the Service User sign-in flow). They do **not** accept Weegloo User tokens, Personal Access Tokens, or DeliveryAccessTokens. Detail: **`weegloo-service-login`** skill.
      - **Current `ServiceUser` (ServiceLogin session):** **`GET https://acma.weegloo.com/v1/me`** with that Bearer Token. **Do not** call **`GET .../v1/spaces/{spaceId}/me`** on ACMA — that URL is **incorrect** for the current member profile. **`auth.weegloo.com`** uses **`/v1/spaces/{spaceId}/...`** for OAuth; **ACMA**’s **`/me`** endpoint is **not** under **`/spaces/{spaceId}`**. Narrative: **`weegloo-service-login`** skill.

  - section: ACMA / ACDA — Content is addressed UNDER its ContentType (no flat /contents)
    items:
      - **Unlike CMA/CDA, ACMA and ACDA have no flat Content endpoints.** Every Content operation is **nested under the ContentType**. Verified against the live OpenAPI specs (see *API documentation* above).
      - **ACMA** (Content CRUD): list/create at **`/v1/spaces/{spaceId}/content-types/{contentTypeId}/contents`**; get/update(PUT/PATCH)/delete at **`/v1/spaces/{spaceId}/content-types/{contentTypeId}/contents/{contentId}`**. There is **no** `/v1/spaces/{spaceId}/contents` and **no** `/v1/spaces/{spaceId}/contents/{contentId}` on ACMA — calling them returns **404**.
      - **ACDA** (Content read): use the same **nested** form — **`/v1/spaces/{spaceId}/content-types/{contentTypeId}/contents`** and **`/v1/spaces/{spaceId}/content-types/{contentTypeId}/contents/{contentId}`**. Even if a flat `/contents` read appears on some ACDA versions, **do not rely on it** — always use the nested form for parity with ACMA and version-independence.
      - **You need the `contentTypeId`.** ACMA/ACDA Content URLs cannot be built from a `contentId` alone. If you only have a `contentId`, obtain its `contentTypeId` from the resource you already hold (e.g. `sys.contentType`) or by listing under the ContentType — never fall back to a flat path.
      - **Wrong (does not exist on ACMA):** `https://acma.weegloo.com/v1/spaces/{spaceId}/contents/{contentId}`.
      - **Correct:** `https://acma.weegloo.com/v1/spaces/{spaceId}/content-types/{contentTypeId}/contents/{contentId}` (ACDA: same path under `https://acda.weegloo.com`).
      - **CMA/CDA contrast:** the flat `/v1/spaces/{spaceId}/contents[...]` style is a **CMA/CDA** convenience — do **not** carry it over to ACMA/ACDA.

  - section: ACMA — ownership and `isAdmin` (app-managed member CRUD scope)
    items:
      - **Default scope:** a `ServiceUser` may CRUD **only the resources they created**. Resources created by other members are not editable or deletable from this member's session.
      - **Cross-member delete via `isAdmin`:** when **`ServiceUser.isAdmin === true`**, that member may **additionally delete** resources created by **other** `ServiceUser`s — **within** the actions permitted by their `ServiceUserRole`. This **adds delete-of-others on top of** the default own-resource CRUD; the member does **not** lose their own-resource capabilities.
      - **`isAdmin` scope is narrow.** It elevates **delete** on others' resources only. It does **not** grant **update** or **read-for-write** on others' resources, and it does **not** elevate the member to a Weegloo console / CMA admin. It also does not enable operations the underlying `ServiceUserRole` does not permit (e.g. if the role cannot delete this `ContentType` at all, `isAdmin` does not unlock it).
      - **Do not** use ACMA to model team-staff editing of the whole Space. That is a **CMA** operation by a Weegloo console user—see the *Service type → API selection* section.

  - section: ACDA — per-member read scope and role overrides
    items:
      - ACDA returns **only** published resources **assigned to** the calling `ServiceUser` (per product/role rules). Unlike CDA (one shared, public, token-scoped read set), ACDA's result set is **per member**.
      - **Per-member customization:** set **`ServiceUser.roleOverride`** to point at a different `ServiceUserRole` to grant a single member access different from `ServiceLogin.sys.defaultRole`—useful for tiered subscriptions, beta cohorts, moderators, etc.
      - **Effective role resolution:** `roleOverride` (if set) wins over `ServiceLogin.sys.defaultRole`. `isAdmin` is **additive** and **narrow**: on **ACMA**, it adds **delete** of other members' resources within the role's permitted operations. It does **not** widen ACDA's per-member read assignment, and it does **not** grant cross-member **update** or **read-for-write** on ACMA.
      - Publish semantics from *CDA — published snapshot only* apply to ACDA as well; see **`weegloo-cda-publish`** skill.

  - section: Weegloo User login — token scope
    items:
      - **Weegloo User** is the Weegloo **platform account** identity (Space owner or **invited** member). **No self-signup** — onboarding is via Space invitation.
      - A Weegloo User Bearer Token (a **Personal Access Token** for servers/CI, or the token returned by the **Weegloo Console FE login popup** for browsers) authorizes **CMA**, **Upload**, and **CDA**.
      - **Do not** ship a Personal Access Token to a browser — it is too privileged and too long-lived. Browser admin UIs use the FE popup mechanism. Mechanics and the popup flow live in **`weegloo-user-login`**.
      - Effective rights on a given Space come from the user's `SpaceRole` via Space membership. Use **`GET /v1/me/space-memberships`** to gate "is this user actually a member of *this* Space?" (see **`weegloo-global-rules`**).
      - For public CDA delivery in production, prefer a least-privilege **`DeliveryAccessToken`** (**`weegloo-delivery-access-token`**) over a Weegloo User Bearer Token — the user token is over-privileged for browser distribution.

  - section: ServiceLogin (Service User) — Bearer Token scope
    items:
      - **`ServiceLogin`** is a per-Space configuration that lets the product run its own end-user (**Service User**) directory (separate from Weegloo platform accounts) — typically via an OAuth provider (Google, etc.). **Anyone may sign up** through it.
      - Resources involved: **`ServiceLogin`** (holds `sys.defaultRole`), **`ServiceUserRole`** (permission rule set for Service Users), **`ServiceUser`** (one per end-user; optional **`roleOverride`** and **`isAdmin`**).
      - A successful ServiceLogin sign-in returns a **Bearer Token** that authorizes **ACMA** and **ACDA** **only**. It is **not** valid for **CMA**, **CDA**, or **Upload**.
      - Do **not** confuse `ServiceUserRole` (Service Users → ACMA / ACDA) with `SpaceRole` (Weegloo Users / `DeliveryAccessToken` → CMA / CDA).
      - Mechanics, configuration, and security details: **`weegloo-service-login`** skill.

  - section: Service type → API selection (decision pointer)
    items:
      - **Public read-only site:** **CDA** with a least-privilege `DeliveryAccessToken` (`SpaceRole`). No ServiceLogin.
      - **Public site + team admin UI:** **CDA** for visitors; **CMA** for the team via **`weegloo-user-login`** (Weegloo User login — PAT for servers, console FE login popup for browsers). No ServiceLogin.
      - **Members-only read service (open end-user sign-up):** **ServiceLogin** + **ACDA**. Configure `ServiceLogin.sys.defaultRole` to a least-privilege `ServiceUserRole`.
      - **Members read + write service (open end-user sign-up):** **ServiceLogin** + **ACMA** (member writes, scoped to own resources; moderators via `isAdmin`) + **ACDA** (member reads). Use **CDA** in addition for any resources that should also be readable by anonymous visitors.
      - **Composite service:** combine the above per caller identity. Each path uses the API matching the caller's identity for that path; tokens **do not** cross identity boundaries.
      - Full recipes, role-budget per service type, and anti-patterns: **`weegloo-service-architecture`** skill.

  - section: CDA requirements (Delivery Access Token)
    items:
      - CDA requires a **Delivery Access Token** (and ACDA its equivalent when using that API—follow **API docs** and env conventions for the project).
      - When **creating** a `DeliveryAccessToken` via CMA (`cma_CreateDeliveryAccessToken`), follow the **`weegloo-delivery-access-token`** skill: **never** bind **Administrator** `SpaceRole`; prefer a **read-only** role for required `ContentType`s only, or **ask the user** to pick a role after listing `SpaceRole`s.
      - **Local Next.js development:** use **`.env.local`** with **`NEXT_PUBLIC_WEEGLOO_DELIVERY_ACCESS_TOKEN`** (and other `NEXT_PUBLIC_WEEGLOO_*` vars) — see `.env.example`.
      - **Weegloo WebHosting (static export):** there is **no server-side `.env`** at request time—CDA and related settings reach the browser via **your build** (for example `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` inlined at build time) or other **project-defined** client config. Document the chosen pattern in the app’s README.

  - section: CMA / ACMA document updates (PATCH, PUT)
    items:
      - For **ContentType**, **Content**, and **Media**, CMA and ACMA REST APIs support **partial updates** via **`PATCH`** using **[RFC 6902 JSON Patch](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6902)** (array of `op` / `path` / `value` / `from` operations, JSON Pointer paths per RFC 6901).
      - For those **`PATCH`** requests, the **`Content-Type`** request header **must** be **`application/json-patch+json`** (not plain `application/json`).
      - **`PUT`** may still be used with the **full** resource body, or — where the OpenAPI contract allows — with a **partial** body containing only the fields or structure you intend to change.
      - Exact **`PATCH`** paths and whether a given **`PUT`** is full or partial replacement are defined per operation in **OpenAPI** on **CMA** / **ACMA**—see **API documentation** section above (`https://docs.weegloo.com/api-docs/cma` or `https://docs.weegloo.com/api-docs/acma`).
      - Agent-oriented detail and usage notes live in the **`weegloo-cma-json-patch`** skill.

  - section: CMA Media list — filter by `mimeGroups` (logical asset type)
    items:
      - On **`GET /v1/spaces/{spaceId}/medias`** (CMA), add a query parameter to keep only assets whose file falls into **one logical category**—e.g. **images**, **video**, **audio**, **PDFs**, **archives**, **code**—instead of listing all Media and filtering in the client.
      - **Parameter shape:** **`fields.file.{locale}.mimeGroups={MimeGroup}`**. The **`{locale}`** segment must match the locale key of the **`fields.file`** map for that space (example: **`fields.file.en-US.mimeGroups=Image`**).
      - **Full URL example (fragment):** **`/v1/spaces/{spaceId}/medias?limit=20&order=-sys.createdAt&fields.file.en-US.mimeGroups=Image`** — prepend the **CMA** base URL from this rule.
      - Pick the **locale** your app uses for **`fields.file`** (often the space **default locale** for a single-locale UI).
      - **Allowed `MimeGroup` enum values** (use the identifier exactly): **`Attachment`**, **`Plaintext`**, **`Image`**, **`Audio`**, **`Video`**, **`RichText`**, **`Presentation`**, **`Spreadsheet`**, **`PdfDocument`**, **`Archive`**, **`Code`**, **`Markup`**.
      - For **pagination**, send **`mimeGroups`** on the **first** request, then follow **`links.next`** so the same filter applies on every page (**`weegloo-list-pagination`** skill).

  - section: Common Mistakes to Avoid
    items:
      - Do not infer or guess URLs. Use only the base URLs listed in this rule.
      - Wrong: `https://cda-weegloo.com` (wrong host pattern), using CMA base URL for CDA traffic.
      - Correct: For CDA content fetch, use `https://cda.weegloo.com/v1/spaces/{spaceId}/...`.
      - Wrong: `Accept: application/json` on Weegloo API requests. Prefer **no** `Accept` header, or **`application/vnd.com.weegloo.v1+json;charset=UTF-8`** if `Accept` is required.
      - Wrong (ACMA/ACDA): flat Content paths like `https://acma.weegloo.com/v1/spaces/{spaceId}/contents/{contentId}` — these **do not exist** on ACMA. Use the nested `…/content-types/{contentTypeId}/contents/{contentId}` form (see *ACMA / ACDA — Content is addressed UNDER its ContentType*).

  - section: Base URL quick reference
    items:
      - CMA: `https://cma.weegloo.com`
      - CDA: `https://cda.weegloo.com`
      - Upload: `https://upload.weegloo.com`
      - ACMA: `https://acma.weegloo.com`
      - ACDA: `https://acda.weegloo.com`
      - Auth (ServiceLogin OAuth): `https://auth.weegloo.com` — see **`weegloo-service-login-sdk`** skill for endpoint paths and the official browser SDK

id: weegloo-default-locale
type: rule
title: Weegloo default locale and per-field locale buckets
description: >
  Locale handling for Content and Media. Before creating or updating localized content,
  invoke the weegloo-default-locale skill for the full playbook.
---

rules:
  - section: Critical invariants (always apply)
    items:
      - Every **Content create** payload must include the **space default locale** value for every populated field. Do not submit creates that populate only non-default locales.
      - **`localized: false`** fields accept a value **only under the default locale** — no other locale buckets allowed.
      - **Always** resolve which locale is the space **default** before authoring multi-locale payloads.
      - **Read fallback is opt-in, not automatic.** A `Locale` falls back only via its **optional `fallbackCode`** (an arbitrary target locale, chainable). A requested locale with **no `fallbackCode`** returns an **empty** value when the field has no entry for it; it does **not** fall back to the default. The default locale is special on **write** (mandatory on create), **not** on read. A `localized: false` field (default bucket only) therefore appears under a non-default locale **only if that locale's `fallbackCode` chain reaches the default**.
      - **Read SHAPE differs by API plane — the #1 locale bug.** **Management (CMA / ACMA)** always returns `fields.{name}` as a **per-locale bucket** → read **`fields.{name}[locale]`**. **Delivery (CDA / ACDA)** by default **flattens** → `fields.{name}` is **the value itself** → read **`fields.{name}`** (indexing `[locale]` gives `undefined`); only **`locale=*`** returns buckets. This holds for **both list and single-content detail** reads, on **CDA and ACDA** alike. Expanded refs come back under a **singular `include`** object keyed by PascalCase type (e.g. **`include.Media`**), and an expanded Media's file URL on a default delivery read is at **`fields.file.url`** (not `fields.file[locale].url`). Full table + a both-shapes accessor: **`weegloo-default-locale`** skill.

  - section: Full guidance
    items:
      - For per-locale bucket semantics, CDA `locale` parameter shapes, read fallback behavior, and write rules, invoke the **`weegloo-default-locale`** skill. This rule is a safety-net summary, not a substitute.

id: weegloo-global-rules
type: rule
title: Weegloo MCP Global Rules
description: >
  These rules apply to all MCP resources and operations, including WebHosting, Content, and ContentType management.
  They are intended to ensure consistent behavior and proper use of MCP tools across all skills.
---

rules:
  - section: Select the working Organization and Space FIRST (hard gate)
    items:
      - **Before any Weegloo work, the working `Organization` and `Space` must be decided.** Almost every resource (ContentType, Content, Media, WebHosting, roles, tokens, …) lives **inside a specific Space**, which lives inside an **Organization**. Choosing the wrong one silently scatters work into an arbitrary workspace.
      - **On the user's FIRST Weegloo request of a session** — any "integrate with Weegloo" / create / update / delete / upload / deploy, or anything that targets a `spaceId` — you **MUST** establish the target Space **before** the first write or space-scoped read. Do **not** start working until it is confirmed.
      - **Do not guess or auto-pick.** Never assume a default, and never use the **first item** from a list of organizations or spaces. If the user did not name a Space, **ask**.
      - **Ask the user to choose one of two paths:** (a) **use an existing** Organization + Space, or (b) **create a new** Organization and/or Space for this work.
      - **To list what the user already has** (so they can choose): organizations via **`GET /me/organization-memberships?include=1`**, spaces via **`GET /me/space-memberships?include=1`** (see *Current User Resources*). Present names/codes and let the user pick — do not pick for them.
      - **To create new:** a `Space` belongs to an `Organization`, so an Organization must be chosen or created **first** (`cma_CreateOrganization`), then the Space (`cma_CreateSpace`). Confirm names with the user before creating.
      - **After it is decided, reuse that `spaceId`** (and Organization) for the rest of the work. If a later request implies a **different** Space, **stop and confirm** the switch rather than silently changing workspace.
      - **Only exempt:** genuinely global, read-only queries that are **not** space-scoped (e.g. listing the user's own organizations/spaces, or `GET /me`). Everything that reads or writes inside a Space is gated.

  - section: When unsure, read the docs first (do not guess)
    items:
      - If you are **not certain** how any Weegloo feature works or behaves — a query/filter parameter, `select`/`include` response shape, locale rules, an error code, publish/version semantics, role/permission scope, or any concept — **look it up in the docs before acting**. Do **not** rely on assumptions or memory.
      - **Where to look — discover the path, do not guess.** Read the general Weegloo docs at **`docs.weegloo.com`**. **First** fetch the index **`https://docs.weegloo.com/llms.txt`**, take the **exact** page path from it (or from a link inside a Weegloo Markdown page you already fetched), then fetch that path with **`.md`** appended. **You may not fetch a `.md` whose path you cannot point to in `llms.txt` (or a real in-doc link)** — do not hand-build, rename, pluralize, or "try" nearby paths; the **`.md`** suffix is not a way to discover paths.
      - **Wrong-path signal:** if a docs fetch returns HTML, a SPA shell (`<!doctype html>` or a `<div id="root">` app root), a redirect to the app, or **403 / 404**, the **path is wrong or absent** — go back to `llms.txt` and re-derive it. Do **not** retry path variants or swap fetch tools to diagnose the same guessed path. Fuller flow and fetch hygiene live in **`weegloo-api-endpoints`**; exact schemas live in the **API Swagger specs**.
      - **Treat the docs as the source of truth** over guesses. After an unexpected error or empty result, re-check the relevant docs page before retrying.

  - section: Read the right skill BEFORE architecture / ContentType design (hard gate)
    items:
      - These rule files are **safety-net summaries, not a substitute** for the skills. Having the rules in context does **not** satisfy this gate — invoke the skill.
      - For any **broad, vague, or "just integrate/connect/use Weegloo" request** that does **not** name a specific feature (e.g. "integrate with Weegloo", "manage my data with Weegloo"), invoke **`weegloo-platform-integration`** FIRST. It maps the plain-language need to the correct concrete skill so the user need not know Weegloo's internal feature names. It only routes — it does **not** replace the gates below.
      - Before proposing or finalizing a **service architecture** (which APIs / login / roles a product uses), you **MUST** invoke **`weegloo-service-architecture`** first. Do **not** decide CMA/CDA vs ACMA/ACDA, token type, or role scope from memory or these summaries.
      - Before configuring **end-user sign-in / sign-up** for a product — creating a **`ServiceLogin`** or a **`ServiceUserRole`**, or scoping **ACMA/ACDA** member access (`createdBy :self`, `isAdmin`, `roleOverride`, `defaultRole`) — you **MUST** invoke **`weegloo-service-login`** (the conceptual model) **first**, and **`weegloo-service-login-sdk`** before wiring the browser OAuth flow (login entry URL vs Google redirect URI, `exchangeToken`, callback). `weegloo-service-architecture` and `weegloo-space-role` only **point to** these skills — reading them, or the SDK skill alone, does **not** satisfy this gate. Do **not** decide the ServiceUser identity model, role scope, or OAuth wiring from memory or these summaries.
      - Before designing or proposing a **ContentType** (fields, `localized`, ShortText/LongText/RichText, validations, `publishWithAuthor`, `Refer`), you **MUST** invoke **`weegloo-create-content-type`** first — and **`weegloo-default-locale`** whenever any field is multi-locale.
      - If the app is a **WebHosting** deploy, invoke **`weegloo-delivery-access-token`** before provisioning any CDA token.
      - Before provisioning **Webhook + WriteBack** for **external API** work (async job Content, `Content.Create` trigger, poll by `sys.id`, LLM/image/search proxy), you **MUST** invoke **`weegloo-webhook-writeback`** first.
      - Before implementing a **file-upload feature in product code** (upload a file, then create a **Media** or **WebHosting** from it), you **MUST** invoke **`weegloo-upload-api`** first. **Do not confuse the two upload paths:** the **Upload REST API** is for the **product's own code**; the **`weegloo-upload` MCP** server is **only** for the **agent/LLM** uploading a local file during a chat (e.g. seeding content, deploying a WebHosting ZIP). Never wire a product to the `weegloo-upload` MCP, and never call the raw REST upload endpoints "via MCP".
      - **Do not ask the user to decide** something a skill already specifies (e.g. LongText vs RichText search semantics) until you have read the relevant skill — research first, then surface only the genuine product choice.

  - section: HTTP JSON media type (when calling Weegloo APIs from code)
    items:
      - Weegloo APIs respond with **`application/vnd.com.weegloo.v1+json;charset=UTF-8`**, not plain `application/json`.
      - Application code (**fetch**, axios, etc.) must **not** send **`Accept: application/json`**; **omit `Accept`** or use the vendor type (see `weegloo-api-endpoints`). Agents normally use **MCP**, not raw HTTP-this applies to **human-written** clients and scripts.

  - section: DeliveryAccessToken and SpaceRole (security)
    items:
      - Follow **`weegloo-delivery-access-token`**. **`cma_CreateDeliveryAccessToken.role.sys.id`** MUST be the **`sys.id`** of the **intended** least-privilege **`SpaceRole`** (e.g. the one created in the same flow for CDA read access, or a **`sys.id`** the user explicitly chose). **Forbidden:** the **first** item from **`cma_GetListSpaceRoles`**, **Administrator**, or switching to Administrator after **`WGL422001`** or any error.
      - **Do not** use **Administrator** for browser-exposed tokens; use **read-only** roles scoped to the needed **`ContentType`s**, or **ask the user** to select **`sys.id`** after listing roles.

  - section: MCP Tool Usage
    items:
      - Always use the designated MCP tools for creating, reading, updating, or deleting resources.
      - Direct API calls or manual edits outside MCP tools, including Swagger or direct HTTP requests, are prohibited.
      - Deploy scripts (e.g. `scripts/deploy-weegloo.mjs`) that call Weegloo APIs directly must NOT be used for deployment. Use MCP tools instead.
      - For human developers performing local development or testing, direct API calls are allowed.

  - section: Current User Resources (Me)
    items:
      - To get the current user's organization list, use GET /me/organization-memberships (NOT /organizations). Use include=1 to fetch organization details (name, code, etc.).
      - To get the current user's space list, use GET /me/space-memberships. Use include=1 to fetch space details (name, code, etc.).
      - Do NOT use /organizations for "my organizations"; use /me/organization-memberships instead.
      - **Response shape — the related resource is nested under `sys`, NOT at the item root.** On a `SpaceMembership` the Space id is at **`item.sys.space.sys.id`** (and on an `OrganizationMembership`, **`item.sys.organization.sys.id`**). Reading the flat path `item.space.sys.id` yields **`undefined`** — a common membership-gate bug where every real member is wrongly rejected. To gate "is this user a member of *this* Space?", match `SPACE_ID` against `item.sys.space.sys.id`. Detail + correct/wrong snippets: **`weegloo-user-login`** skill.

  - section: ACMA / ACDA Content paths are nested under ContentType (no flat /contents)
    items:
      - On **ACMA** and **ACDA**, every Content operation **MUST** address the Content **under its ContentType**: list/create at **`/v1/spaces/{spaceId}/content-types/{contentTypeId}/contents`**, and get/update/delete at **`/v1/spaces/{spaceId}/content-types/{contentTypeId}/contents/{contentId}`**.
      - **The CMA/CDA-style flat Content paths do NOT exist on ACMA** — never call **`/v1/spaces/{spaceId}/contents`** or **`/v1/spaces/{spaceId}/contents/{contentId}`** on **ACMA** (they return **404**). On **ACDA**, use the same **nested** form for parity and reliability — do **not** assume a flat `/contents` path is available.
      - You must know the **`contentTypeId`** to address a Content on ACMA/ACDA. If you only hold a `contentId`, resolve its ContentType first (from the resource you already have, or by listing under the ContentType) — do **not** fall back to a flat path.
      - **Wrong:** `https://acma.weegloo.com/v1/spaces/{spaceId}/contents/{contentId}`. **Correct:** `https://acma.weegloo.com/v1/spaces/{spaceId}/content-types/{contentTypeId}/contents/{contentId}`.
      - This is an **application-code** rule (ACMA/ACDA are called from product code, not by the agent over MCP). Base URLs and the full ACMA/ACDA contrast live in **`weegloo-api-endpoints`**.

  - section: Resource Search
    items:
      - List endpoints share common query params — `limit`, `skip`, `order`, `include`, `select`, `filter`. **Shapes, defaults, and examples are canonical at https://docs.weegloo.com/api/reference/common/query-parameters — read it rather than guessing.**
      - Tripwires for application code (enforced server-side, easy to get wrong):
          - `limit`: **hard max 100** — a larger value is rejected. To read more, page via `links.next`; never hardcode 200/500/1000.
          - `skip`: do NOT use for paging — use cursors (`next`/`prev`, see Pagination Handling).
          - `include=1` resolves related resources (e.g. `createdBy`); `select` projects fields — see the reference above.
          - **References are NEVER embedded.** A Content does **not** carry its Media (or any linked Content/Space/Organization/User) inline — a reference field holds only a stub `{ "sys": { "id": "abc", "type": "Refer", "targetType": "Media" } }`. To get the real resource: (a) read `sys.id` and fetch it (e.g. `GET .../medias/{id}`), or (b) pass `?include=1` and read it from the response's **singular `include` object keyed by PascalCase `targetType`** (`include.Media`, `include.Content`, `include.User`, …). Do **not** assume `fields.image`/`fields.file`/an author already hold the asset URL or the linked document. Detail: **`weegloo-api-query-optimization`** / **`weegloo-default-locale`** skills.

  - section: Pagination Handling
    items:
      - After requesting a list of resources, the response body (JSON) contains a `links` object with `next` and `prev` properties.
      - `links.next`: Full path for the next page (e.g., /v1/market/apps?limit=6&order=-sys.createdAt,sys.id&next=CURSOR). If absent, there are no more pages.
      - `links.prev`: Full path for the previous page. If absent, there is no previous page.
      - To fetch the next page, use the `next` query parameter value from `links.next` (extract from the URL) and pass it as the `next` param in your next request. Alternatively, call the full path in `links.next` directly.
      - Do NOT use `skip`; pagination is cursor-based only.

  - section: Resource Updates
    items:
      - When updating any resource, always include the `x-weegloo-version` header with the current resource's `sys.version`.
      - **MCP update tools take the version via the parameter named `X-Weegloo-Version`** (matching the HTTP header, capitalized exactly) — NOT `version` or `xWeeglooVersion`. Guessing the wrong param name leaves the version stale and the update is rejected as a version conflict.
      - **Updates are FULL REPLACEMENT:** resend ALL fields, not just the changed ones. On a version conflict, GET the resource to read the current `sys.version`, then retry the update with that fresh version.
      - All resource updates must use the appropriate MCP tool; direct modifications outside MCP tools are not allowed.

  - section: Optional Guidance
    items:
      - Always verify that `index.html` remains at the root when re-uploading or updating WebHosting resources.

  - section: WebHosting platform limits
    items:
      - **Applies only to Weegloo WebHosting** as the deploy target-not to apps self-hosted on other platforms.
      - **Static sites only:** no SSR or app server on the host-ship a **pre-built** static export (see `weegloo-web-hosting-rules`).
      - **Weegloo REST from a WebHosted site:** the **browser** must call Weegloo REST APIs such as **CDA** (**`fetch` / AJAX**); there is no server on Weegloo to do it per request. Elsewhere-hosted apps may use SSR or server-side clients as they choose.
      - **At most 100 files** per deployment ZIP; prefer **web fonts** from CDNs (see `weegloo-web-hosting-rules`).

  - section: Filter Parameters (API List Endpoints)
    items:
      - Filters are direct query params (NOT wrapped in `filter[]`), e.g. `name[prefix]=value`. **Format, the full operator set, and per-field-type support are canonical at https://docs.weegloo.com/api/reference/common/query-parameters — read it rather than guessing operators** (an unsupported operator is rejected).
      - **Tripwire — Refer fields:** can't filter Content by a Refer field's target via `fields.<refer>.sys.id[eq]`. Use `sys.id[in]=…` (`weegloo-api-query-optimization`) or fetch the set and group client-side.
      - **Tripwire — `fields.*` on the flat `/contents` list needs ContentType scope (CDA & CMA):** to filter or sort the flat `/contents` list by any `fields.*`, scope the type with `sys.contentType.sys.id=<id>` (a bare `contentType=<id>` is not enough). NOT needed on the nested `/content-types/{id}/contents` form or on ACMA/ACDA (the path already carries the type). Wrong: `…/contents?contentType=<CT>&fields.status=active`; correct: `…/contents?sys.contentType.sys.id=<CT>&fields.status=active` (`weegloo-api-query-optimization`).
      - **Tripwire — search locus (in-memory vs server-side):** a UI search box is **not** automatically an in-memory `Array.filter`. Filtering the loaded array is correct **only when that array already holds the WHOLE dataset**; over a paginated, large, or unknown-size list (e.g. *all* Media in a Space — the visible rows are not the dataset) it searches only loaded rows and silently misses the rest. In that case search **server-side** via the list API + `links.next`, not in memory.
      - **Tripwire — full-text search on `fields.*`:** plain `eq` on a text field is **exact** match. For partial/fuzzy "contains" full-text over `fields.*` text (and the `regex` / geo `near`/`within` operators) send the header **`X-Weegloo-Advanced-Search: true`** (then `eq` on a full-text-enabled LongText matches items that *contain* the term). RichText/Json fields are **not** searchable — make a field searchable at modeling time (`weegloo-create-content-type`). Detail: **`weegloo-api-query-optimization`**.

id: weegloo-media-lifecycle
type: rule
title: Weegloo Media - sys.status, file processing, and safe use from Content
description: >
  Media sys.status and fields.file locale state; automatic processing and transition to Published;
  wait before referencing from Content; unpublish before delete. CMA/MCP and app code.
---

rules:
  - section: Media `sys.status` (exactly one of)
    items:
      - **`Draft`**: Not published - **unpublished** editorial state.
      - **`Changed`**: Was published; the asset has **local modifications** not yet reflected in the published view (republish workflow may apply per product/API).
      - **`Published`**: Published and **no pending unpublished edits** relative to that published snapshot.
      - **`Archived`**: Archived (treated as archived in the product lifecycle).

  - section: Media `fields.file.{locale}.state` (per locale file)
    items:
      - **`null`** or the **`file` / locale bucket absent** for that aspect: **processing finished successfully** for that file representation (ready from the processor’s perspective).
      - **`PENDING`**: Queued; the system has **not** started processing yet.
      - **`PROCESSING`**: The system is **actively processing** the file.
      - **`FAILED`**: Processing **errored**; do not treat the asset as deliverable until the failure is addressed.

  - section: Create → automatic processing → `Published` (no mandatory manual Publish for the happy path)
    items:
      - After **Media** is **created**, the platform **automatically** runs the **processing pipeline** for **all** relevant **`file`** locale entries.
      - When **processing completes successfully**, Weegloo **automatically** moves **`sys.status`** to **`Published`**-you **do not** rely on the author **calling a separate Publish API** just to reach **`Published`** after a normal create+process flow.
      - **Before** attaching a **Refer → Media** from **Content** (or assuming CDA-safe delivery), **wait** until **`sys.status === Published`** (and confirm **`file.{locale}.state`** is not **`PENDING`**, **`PROCESSING`**, or **`FAILED`** for the locales you care about). Polling GET Media or equivalent is the usual pattern in app code (e.g. **`lib/weegloo/cma-media-upload.ts`**).
      - **Do not** equate “safe to use” with “user clicked Publish”: for new uploads, **“wait until Published”** means **wait for the system** to finish processing and set status-**not** “always invoke **`cma_PublishOneMedia`** manually.” Manual publish may still exist for other transitions (e.g. **`Draft`** / **`Changed`** workflows); follow OpenAPI for those cases.

  - section: Using Media from Content (summary)
    items:
      - **Requirement:** reference only when the Media is **deliverable** - typically **`sys.status`** is **`Published`** and file **`state`** indicates **completion** (see above).
      - This is **not** a separate human step after every upload in the default pipeline; it is **readiness gating** (poll/wait).

  - section: Delete order
    items:
      - **Unpublish** (or move out of a published state per API rules) **before** **delete** when the API requires it-do not assume delete replaces unpublish.
      - **`Archived`** is a distinct lifecycle state; follow CMA/OpenAPI for whether delete is allowed from **`Archived`** vs requires another transition.

  - section: LLM summary
    items:
      - **Statuses:** `Draft` | `Changed` | `Published` | `Archived` on **`sys.status`**.
      - **File states:** `null`/missing = done; **`PENDING`** / **`PROCESSING`** / **`FAILED`** = not done or error.
      - **After create:** system processes files → on success **`sys.status`** becomes **`Published`** automatically - **wait/poll**, don’t teach “always call Publish” as the default post-upload step.
      - **Before Content references:** wait until **`Published`** + acceptable **`file.*.state`**.
      - **Delete:** **Unpublish** (or required precursor) → **Delete** when the API demands it.

id: weegloo-web-hosting-rules
type: rule
title: Weegloo WebHosting Rules
description: >
  WebHosting deployment constraints. Before any deploy to Weegloo WebHosting,
  invoke the weegloo-web-hosting skill for the full workflow.
---

rules:
  - section: Critical constraints (always apply)
    items:
      - **Static hosting only.** No SSR, no server runtime. Frameworks must build to static export.
      - **Max 100 files** in the deployed ZIP. Prefer CDN web fonts over self-hosted.
      - **`index.html` at ZIP root.** Nested structures not allowed.
      - **MCP tools only** for deployment. No deploy scripts, no direct API calls.
      - **Subdomain is auto-chosen by the LLM — never ask the user.** Pick a **distinctive** subdomain that fits the service (not a plain common noun, which collides); the user can change it anytime later. After deploy, inform the user of the chosen subdomain and that it is changeable.
      - **`CheckSubdomain` before `CreateWebHosting`.** Always. On collision, auto-pick another distinctive variant and re-check — do not ask the user.

  - section: Full workflow
    items:
      - For the complete deploy flow (build → verify → ZIP → Upload → CreateWebHosting → poll), redeploy via UpdateOneWebHosting, and static export configuration, invoke the **`weegloo-web-hosting`** skill. This rule is a safety-net summary, not a substitute.
